o1.biggest_strength: It reads the data well: leads with dark spots, segments by quiz answer, teaches slow starts, and gives sunscreen its own objection-handling email using the white-cast review.
o1.biggest_mistake: The customer-facing copy uses the banned/off-brand word “brightening” and assumes a 14-day code expiry that must be enforced before this can run.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the banned language, verify the expiry and sunscreen texture claims, and make the final routine safer by not pushing the acid wash twice daily for everyone.

o2.biggest_strength: It turns the key signals into a calm, segmented flow: one product per quiz answer, slow-start education, and a strong sunscreen email that answers white cast and humidity doubts.
o2.biggest_mistake: It assumes no coupon deadline, so it misses the potentially high-value expiry reminder the owner hoped for if the 10% code is time-limited.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an enforced code-deadline reminder if the offer has one, and replace the remaining implementation placeholders with final dynamic product links.

reason: I would rather hand Output 2 to the team because it is cleaner on brand, safer on claims, and avoids fake urgency while still acting on the data. Output 1 is very useful, but the banned word and assumed expiry need more careful cleanup before launch.
